summary:
Radar, 19 Oct 2026. Retatrutide is still the strongest lane, and it got stronger this weekend. CBS News, picked up by NY Post, Futurism and Gizmodo, reported that the FDA has received at least two reports of deaths after people used products sold as retatrutide. The FDA hasn't said whether it verified them. Lilly's CMO called black-market product "not a medicine". Lilly said in July it plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027, so the drug is not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026. Two Shorts fit this: the dated status question (our best Instagram format) and "why a vial labelled retatrutide isn't the trial drug". Both must be calm, attributed to the FDA or Lilly, and must never name a seller.

The best fresh study is the ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 records analysis of about 2.03 million surgical patients. GLP-1 users had 11% lower odds of major heart complications and 8% lower odds of infections after surgery. It's observational and the authors say it shows association, not cause. That builds on our anesthesia Short (83 views). Mainstream pickup is only Medical Xpress and Inside Precision Medicine so far, so we're early.

Head-to-head demand is steady. Search-query feeds show "tirzepatide vs semaglutide" and "most effective weight loss drug 2026". Novo's lawsuit, which argues SURMOUNT-5 didn't test the newer Wegovy 7.2 mg dose, gives SURMOUNT-5 follow-ups a fresh angle. Alcohol and addiction is rising again (News-Medical Oct 19, Medical Economics, the VA CRAVE trial). Sleep apnea and PCOS are fresh-study hooks. Orforglipron and CagriSema belong in long-form decoders only.

Rejected: compounded or telehealth price-cut stories (Mochi), switching from compounded drugs, and the anorexia/telehealth-loophole stories. I couldn't verify the PCOS meta-analysis, the UK price-rise study or the ScienceAlert fat-cell injection directly (PubMed pages were blocked), so writers must pull the primary sources before scripting. The Zepbound KwikPen "approval" headline in the feed is old news (Jan/Feb 2026), so I skipped it.

candidates.topic: Is retatrutide approved yet? (Oct 2026). Not FDA-approved; Lilly plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027 after positive Phase 3 (TRIUMPH) results, while the FDA has received at least two death reports involving products sold as retatrutide (unverified)
candidates.angle: Calm, dated status check: 'Is retatrutide approved yet? (Oct 2026)'. Answer 'No' by about 5 s. Lilly says it plans to file in early 2027. Explain why that means approval is unlikely before late 2027. Explain why FDA death reports are a warning sign, not proof of cause. End with: talk to your prescriber about approved options. Never name sellers.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–10 days (news cycle plus Lilly Q3 earnings)
candidates.why_now: CBS News reported FDA death reports (amplified by NY Post Oct 16, Futurism Oct 17 and Gizmodo). Lilly has stepped up lawsuits. Google News has many search-query feeds like 'retatrutide approval status' and 'fda concerns unapproved glp-1 drugs retatrutide'. This is our best lane (median 98 views), and the dated status question is our best Instagram format (85 reach).

evidence.source: Gizmodo (CBS News report on FDA death reports)
evidence.signal: FDA received at least two reports of deaths linked to products claiming to be retatrutide; details unverified, causation unclear
Inside retatrutide's black market, Lilly's six lawsuits and a brewing FDA battle
Retatrutide met Phase 3 weight-loss endpoints in 2 obesity trials (Jul 23, 2026)
Two people died after taking bootleg 'triple G' (Oct 16)

candidates.topic: Why a vial labelled 'retatrutide' isn't the trial drug: Lilly warns illicit products may have the wrong dose or the wrong ingredient; reported seized samples contained other substances such as insulin
candidates.angle: 'Is bootleg retatrutide the same as Lilly's drug?' A plain explainer: what a clinical trial controls (verified product, dose, monitoring) versus an unverified vial. Quote Lilly's printed warning word for word and date it. No fear-bait, no sellers, no how-to. Point to a prescriber and FDA-approved options.
candidates.why_now: Lilly's CMO said black-market retatrutide is 'not a medicine' (Stocktwits, Oct 18). The death-report story is spreading, and Reddit discussion continues after the Penn analysis of 13,589 users.

evidence.signal: Lilly files six new lawsuits; CMO says black-market drug is 'not a medicine' (Oct 18)
Lilly cracks down on the illicit retatrutide black market
Black-market retatrutide linked to multiple deaths (Oct 17)

candidates.topic: On a GLP-1 before surgery? ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 records analysis of ~2.03 million adults having elective surgery: GLP-1 users (145,610) had 11% lower odds of major heart complications and 8% lower odds of infections after surgery (observational)
candidates.angle: 'Does Ozempic or Mounjaro change surgery risk?' Lead with the encouraging association, then the hedge ('linked to', not 'causes'; the authors say more research is needed). Add the practical line: tell your surgical and anesthesia team you take a GLP-1 and follow their instructions. No stopping advice from us.
candidates.why_now: Medical Xpress and Inside Precision Medicine covered it on Oct 18. Recent orthopedic papers (knee, shoulder, spine) plus a Yahoo orthopedic-surgeon piece show steady demand. Our anesthesia Short got 83 views, above the median. Few creators have covered it yet.

evidence.signal: 2,028,601 patients (Epic Cosmos, 2016–2024); 11% lower odds of major cardiovascular complications and 8% lower odds of infections; authors stress it's correlational
GLP-1 use before knee replacement linked to lower post-op heart attack, DVT and VTE rates (Oct 15)
Safety of GLP-1 use in non-diabetic patients having shoulder replacement

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide: did SURMOUNT-5 test the highest Wegovy dose? Novo's lawsuit says Lilly's ads rely on SURMOUNT-5 (semaglutide 1.7/2.4 mg) and ignore Wegovy 7.2 mg (approved Mar 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide vs semaglutide: which doses were actually compared?' Name both drugs and put each dose next to every number. Population: adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks. Say clearly there is no head-to-head trial against 7.2 mg. Attribute the lawsuit's claims to Novo, as allegations. Include 'don't switch or stop on your own'.
keywords: which is better mounjaro or ozempic
candidates.why_now: Google News query feeds show 'best weight loss drug 2026 tirzepatide vs semaglutide' and a 'most effective… comparison' query (Oct 19). The Novo vs Lilly ad lawsuit is resurfacing (Stocktwits, Oct 18). The SURMOUNT-5 Short is our second-best at 157 views and still growing.

evidence.signal: Novo sued Lilly over GLP-1 ads; it says the ads compare top Zepbound doses with lower Wegovy doses and leave out the 7.2 mg data
Novo Nordisk sues Eli Lilly over 'misleading' GLP-1 advertising
Novo lawsuit against Lilly back in the news Oct 18

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide: which had more stomach side effects in SURMOUNT-5? (adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks)
candidates.angle: A follow-up head-to-head with both drug names first. Put each GI side-effect rate next to its drug. Most cases were mild to moderate and happened while the dose was going up. Add habits that help: smaller meals, eating slowly, fluids unless you've been told to limit them. Add 'don't switch or stop on your own'.
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; refreshed by the head-to-head news cycle
candidates.why_now: Seen in 11 snapshots with steady momentum. The comparison queries are live this week, and our proven playbook is head-to-heads that name both drugs.

evidence.signal: 'best weight loss drug 2026 tirzepatide vs semaglutide' (Oct 19)
SURMOUNT-5 at the centre of the Novo vs Lilly ad dispute

candidates.topic: Did retatrutide beat tirzepatide? A decoder of TRIUMPH Phase 3 and TRIUMPH-2 results ahead of Lilly's Q3 earnings, with the planned Q1 2027 FDA filing
candidates.angle: Long-form in our breakout format: 'Did retatrutide beat tirzepatide? [one number]'. Say there is no head-to-head trial and explain cross-trial caveats. Cover how the triple-hormone mechanism (GLP-1, GIP, glucagon) works, trial populations, the common GI side effects and the dated status. Close with a gray-market warning and a prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Several query feeds this week: 'retatrutide weight loss compared to other drugs', 'eli lilly new weight loss drug retatrutide' and 'most effective weight loss drug 2026 tirzepatide retatrutide'. Long-form decoders of new drugs are our only long-form that travels (median ~32 views, EloraTZP 396).

evidence.signal: 5 things to know about retatrutide (Aug 14, 2026)
Lilly will file retatrutide for FDA approval in early 2027 (announced at Q2 earnings, Jul 23)
'retatrutide weight loss compared to other drugs' (Oct 16)

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide (Ozempic) reduce drinking? Lancet-family RCT in alcohol use disorder with obesity (2.4 mg weekly, 26 weeks, heavy drinking days cut by ~13.7 percentage points vs placebo), oral-semaglutide trial (50 adults, 8 weeks), new Addictive Behaviors review and the VA CRAVE trial
candidates.angle: Encouraging but honest: 'Does Ozempic curb drinking? What 2 trials found'. Explain the brain's reward pathway. Small trials; not approved for alcohol use disorder. If drinking is a concern, talk to a clinician.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical published an addiction-mechanisms explainer on Oct 19. Medical Economics ran 'semaglutide cuts heavy drinking' on Oct 17. The Addictive Behaviors review (Oct 10) and the VA CRAVE trial start keep it in the news. Alcohol is a big seasonal theme going into the holidays.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide 2.4 mg for 26 weeks cut heavy drinking days by an estimated 13.7 percentage points vs placebo (AUD with obesity)
Review of clinical efficacy and mechanisms (Oct 10)
How GLP-1 drugs may help treat addiction (Oct 19)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Zepbound) and sleep apnea: can weight loss on a GLP-1 change your CPAP needs? SURMOUNT-OSA plus a new narrative review on de-escalating OSA therapy after GLP-1 weight loss
candidates.angle: 'Does Zepbound help sleep apnea?' Cover SURMOUNT-OSA (moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity) and the US approval for OSA. The review says any change to CPAP happens only after re-testing with your sleep doctor. Never 'ditch your CPAP'.
keywords: can I stop cpap on zepbound
candidates.why_now: News-Medical published an OSA explainer on Oct 19. There's a query feed for 'fda approves zepbound for obstructive sleep apnea'. The Cureus de-escalation review (Sep 17) is a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: De-escalating OSA therapy after GLP-1-induced weight loss: narrative review
GLP-1 drugs and OSA explainer (Oct 19)

candidates.topic: Are GLP-1 pills as effective as injections? Oral semaglutide (Wegovy pill) and orforglipron (Foundayo) vs the shots, Oct 2026
candidates.angle: Long-form decoder (orforglipron Shorts underperform). Compare each pill with its own trial results, food and water rules, and who it's approved for, by country and dated. EU orforglipron: CHMP recommended it; Commission decision pending. Include the common GI side effects and 'don't switch on your own'.
keywords: are glp-1 pills as effective as injections
how effective is the wegovy pill
candidates.why_now: Query feeds this week: 'are the glp 1 pills as effective as injections' and 'how effective is the wegovy pill'. Coverage includes Medscape's orforglipron explainer (Oct 16), Fierce Pharma's oral GLP-1 tracker, Bahrain's Wegovy pill approval and Amazon Pharmacy stocking it. New pill research is a long-form-friendly pillar.

evidence.signal: What to know about the GLP-1 pill orforglipron (Oct 16)
Lilly's weight-loss pill wins EU regulator's backing (Oct 16)
GRADE meta-analysis of heart outcomes with oral incretin drugs in type 2 diabetes (67,679 patients)

candidates.topic: Did CagriSema beat semaglutide? New systematic review and meta-analysis (Front Endocrinol, Oct 2) of CagriSema vs semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight/obesity with or without type 2 diabetes, plus the 'should amylin have been the target?' debate
candidates.angle: Long-form decoder: 'Did CagriSema beat semaglutide? [one number]'. Explain amylin simply (fullness hormone). Report the pooled extra weight loss and GI side effects, with populations by diabetes status. Date its regulatory status and attribute it to Novo.
candidates.why_now: BioSpace published an amylin feature on Oct 19, there's a fresh meta-analysis, and there's a 'new weight loss drugs 2026 retatrutide cagrisema' query feed. Next-gen decoders are our long-form winners.

evidence.signal: CagriSema vs semaglutide 2.4 mg: systematic review, meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis
Should amylin have been obesity therapeutics' primary target? (Oct 19)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines vs metformin for pregnancy rates in women with PCOS: new systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials (Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol, Oct 15)
candidates.angle: 'Can GLP-1 medicines help with PCOS?' Use the pooled RCT result with its exact hedge, then the essential safety line: semaglutide and tirzepatide aren't for use in pregnancy, so planning a pregnancy is a conversation to have with your doctor. No stopping or timing instructions from us. Pull the numbers from the full text first (the abstract couldn't be fetched).
candidates.why_now: A fresh RCT meta-analysis lands on a hugely searched 'Ozempic babies' and PCOS conversation. There's also a Nature piece on digital GLP-1 care in women (Oct 16) and an eligibility paper on reproductive-age women. Little evidence-based coverage so far.

evidence.source: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol (PubMed)
evidence.signal: Meta-analysis of RCTs: GLP-1 RAs vs metformin on pregnancy rates in PCOS (Oct 15)
Real-world digital-first delivery of GLP-1 therapy in women (Oct 16)

candidates.topic: Is 'Ozempic face' real? New systematic review on facial changes linked to GLP-1 medicines (Aesthetic Plast Surg, Oct 12) as Lilly explores aesthetic medicine
candidates.angle: Positive and non-shaming: 'Does Ozempic change your face?' Facial volume loss follows weight loss in general, not a unique drug effect, based on what the review actually says. Add muscle- and skin-friendly habits (protein, strength training, steady pace) without promising results. No before/after images.
candidates.why_now: A new systematic review plus Lilly's aesthetic-medicine push (Daily Journal, Oct 18). 'Ozempic face' is a perennial top search.

evidence.signal: Facial remodelling associated with GLP-1 RAs: systematic review (Oct 12)
Lilly explores aesthetic medicine as patients cope with GLP-1 weight-loss effects (Oct 18)

candidates.topic: What happened when Mounjaro's UK price went up? Real-world treatment patterns and weight outcomes in over 1 million self-paying UK adults with overweight or obesity (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 14)
candidates.angle: For UK viewers: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): what happened after the UK price rise?' Report the actual findings on who stayed on treatment and weight outcomes. Tie it to what the evidence says about keeping results (SURMOUNT-4). Add 'don't stop or change doses on your own; talk to your prescriber'. Pull numbers from the full text (abstract not fetched).
candidates.why_now: It's a very large real-world dataset on a pain point our UK audience shares. Links to the 'stopping tirzepatide' topic, which has been rising for 5 snapshots.

evidence.signal: Treatment patterns and weight outcomes before and after a tirzepatide price increase in over 1M self-paying UK adults

candidates.topic: Will Ozempic and Wegovy cost less in 2027? Novo's announced US list-price cuts of up to 50% from 2027, a new Wegovy subscription model, and open-enrollment coverage changes
candidates.angle: 'Will Wegovy cost less in 2027?' Explain the difference between the list price and what you pay. Only FDA-approved products through licensed pharmacies, with prescriber and insurer questions to ask. Never mention compounded or telehealth discount sellers.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics covered the Wegovy subscription model (Oct 18) and the up-to-50% price cuts (Oct 16). Open enrollment is starting now. Note: our coverage/cost carousel reached 0, so make this a Short.

evidence.signal: Novo to cut Ozempic and Wegovy prices up to 50% in 2027 (Oct 16)
Novo Nordisk launches Wegovy subscription model (Oct 18)

candidates.topic: Can a new injection stop weight regain after GLP-1s? Early research on an injection that makes fat cells self-destruct (ScienceAlert, Oct 18), set against SURMOUNT-4 regain data
candidates.angle: 'Is there a fix for weight regain after Ozempic?' Lead with what's proven (SURMOUNT-4: continued treatment kept weight off better than switching to placebo). Present the fat-cell injection only as early-stage lab research, likely animal (verify), with no human results yet.
candidates.why_now: The ScienceAlert headline (Oct 18) is viral-shaped. 'Stopping' and regain topics are rising across 5 snapshots. The primary study hasn't been verified yet.

evidence.signal: New injection makes fat cells self-destruct and might prevent GLP-1 weight regain (Oct 18)

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide cause breast cancer? Rising search question
candidates.angle: Only if it's done as a calm myth-check citing the label and trial safety data, and only if the evidence is clear. Our data show scare topics about approved drugs underperform (pancreatic cancer 25, NAION 32). Low priority.
candidates.why_now: Google News query feed shows the question (Oct 18), but there's no new study behind it.

evidence.signal: 'does tirzepatide cause breast cancer' (Oct 18)

candidates.angle: Do not cover. It promotes a telehealth or compounded source, which our guardrails ban.
